reviews.title: I can no longer trust Clue
reviews.text:
used Clue for about a decade, but I have finally deleted it. Over the years, its Apple Health synchronization repeatedly failed or worked only intermittently, leaving serious gaps in years of important menstrual health records even though all permissions and settings were correct.

While looking for another way to restore the records that Clue had failed to sync, I unexpectedly discovered an even more alarming problem in earlier years. Clue had repeatedly written duplicate period records to Apple Health. In some individual years, there were more than 10,000 menstrual flow entries.

I ultimately had to export my Clue data, remove the incomplete and duplicated records from Apple Health, and rebuild my entire history using another app. This is completely unacceptable for an app entrusted with sensitive health information. After this experience, I simply cannot trust Clue with my health data anymore.

reviews.title: I’ve used Clue for 10 years

reviews.title: Was good a decade ago. Now it’s just sloppy self-promotion.
reviews.text: I downloaded Clue 12(!) years ago, and I really loved it at the time. Simple interface, lots of options to collect data without too many unnecessary bells and whistles. But the years, it’s gotten SO incessant about badgering you to upgrade to the paid app. There are constant banners and pop-ups trying to get you to subscribe, and the other features are just visual clutter. The completely unnecessary “content” tab irks me on particular—who the hell is going to their period tracker to listen to a podcast? Why would I want to read testimonials from members dressed up as heartwarming stories about female empowerment?? It also DOES sell your data to third party services (albeit anonymized). I understand they’re a company but they’ve clearly gotten too big for their britches, prioritized profit, and the product is not good enough to justify it. I’ll just using my own damn calendar.
